messages.author: ac859c12d81dd7f6
messages.subject: factored boxplot with jitter
parts:
Combining geom_boxplot with geom_jitter is a nice way to do a
visualization. It's also nice to have side-by-side boxplots based on a
factor. However, when jitter is combined with side-by-side boxplots,
the jittered points do not respect the factor.

ggplot(mydf) +
geom_boxplot() +
aes(x=myfactor, y=dependent, fill=treatment) +
geom_jitter(aes(colour=treatment))

Notice that the points colored as some treatment occur not just in the
x-axis space dedicated to the boxplot of that treatment, but also in
the x-axis space dedicated to the boxplot of the other treatment.

Yes, because the jittered points don't know anything about the
boxplots and how much space they take up. They may be work-arounds,
but it's difficult to know without a reproducible example...

messages.author: ac859c12d81dd7f6
messages.subject: Re: factored boxplot with jitter
parts:
No workaround necessary (for me, for right now)... But glad to know
that you understand what the problem is.

Example:

> p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(factor(cyl), mpg))
> p + geom_boxplot(aes(fill = factor(am))) + geom_jitter(aes(colour=factor(am)))

This just combines a couple of examples from

http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_boxplot.html

You might want to clarify the documentation that geom_jitter may give
misleading results when combined with geom_boxplot.
